prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
I can’t reliably name one single “best” roofing company for every situation, because the right contractor depends on your needs (roof type, budget, insurance claim status, timeline) and on recent local performance. I can, however, give a practical plan and criteria to pick the best roofer in Dallas and help you vet candidates.

Quick checklist to find the best Dallas roofing company
- Get 3 written estimates (same scope/materials) so you can compare apples-to-apples.
- Verify insurance: ask for current general liability and workers’ compensation certificates and call the carrier to confirm.
- Confirm local presence: a Dallas-based or long-established contractor will be easier to contact for callbacks/warranty work.
- Ask about warranties: manufacturer (shingle) warranty and contractor workmanship warranty — get both in writing.
- Check reviews/history: Google, Yelp, Angi, BBB, and local Facebook groups. Ask for recent local references and photos of finished jobs.
- Confirm permits and inspections: contractor should pull all required city permits and handle inspections.
- Payment terms: avoid large up-front payments. Typical: small deposit, progress payments, final payment on completion and lien waivers.
- Materials & scope: make sure the bid includes roof deck repairs, underlayment type, ventilation, flashing replacement, and disposal of old materials.
- Beware storm-chasers: after storms you’ll see out-of-area crews. Prefer contractors with a local office and established Dallas references.

Red flags
- No proof of insurance or unwillingness to provide certificates.
- High-pressure sales tactics or insisting on cash-only large deposits.
- Vague or unsigned scope of work, or no written warranty.
- Very low price compared to other bids (could mean cutting corners or surprise change orders).

How I can help next
- If you tell me: your address/area in Dallas (or neighborhood), roof type (asphalt, metal, tile), approximate size, and whether this is an insurance claim, I can give tailored questions to ask and a prioritized shortlist approach.
- If you want, I can also draft an email/template to send to contractors for consistent quotes, and a comparison table you can use to evaluate bids.

If you’d like, tell me your neighborhood or a little about your roof and I’ll help you next step (sample questions, contract checklist, or a short template to request quotes).
